Director seat, summon #25, `session_012GcsUbuqFGBibkEDMRC1eE`. Presented in detail with the recommendation A (unify to the guarded resolver, census first); the maintainer agreed and then **amended it in four sentences**, quoted verbatim above. The amendment outranks the seat's presentation (「维护者裁决 > …」) and this record executes the amended ruling. Thread re-read to its last comment (5748865537) in the act that wrote this.

## Ruling — A′: one implementation, the console's `/` behaviour is the fixed point, no census, no third-party customisation surface

- **The console's current `/` routing does not change.** The compiled console (`apps/console` built and consumed by objectstack through the usual refresh) must answer `/` exactly as it does today — `app.isDefault` honoured, objectui#4048's single-visible-app heuristic and objectui#4233's refusal to conclude from an unresolved list both kept. That is the acceptance: the console build's existing `/` tests and the parity instrument `homeAffordancesFollowDeclaration-7256` stay green, unchanged.
- **Two implementations become one — in whichever direction is less code.** Either the guarded logic (`RootLandingRedirect` + `resolveLandingPath`) becomes the package's `RootRedirect` and `apps/console` mounts it from there, or the unguarded published twin is removed and the shell takes the console's element; the dev picks the direction with the smaller diff and says so in one line in the PR. ⛔ Not both kept (B refused: 「怎么简化怎么处理」). ⛔ Not unified to the unguarded one (C refused: it changes the console).
- **No census.** The maintainer's reading: third-party projects are not visible from here, so a consumer census reads nothing (「普查没有意义」). The seat's "first deliverable" clause is withdrawn.
- **No third-party customisation surface.** No prop, option or documented extension point for a custom `/` resolver is designed (「没有需求让第三方开发者做自定义」). The console's only current use is the compiled artefact objectstack consumes; the published package's `/` default has no separate requirement.

Four-facet reading (this seat's own, re-read under the amendment): ① one implementation, and it is the one the product actually ships — the facet holds; ② the only measured consumer is objectstack's compiled console, and its behaviour is pinned as the fixed point — the facet is now answered, not open; ③ no consumer can receive a default different from the console's, because there is only one; ④ strictly smaller than the seat's A: no census, no customisation surface, no changeset narrative about external consumers beyond the package's normal convention.

`Prior rulings read: objectui#7373 ruling B (recovery redirects, ⛔ not the landing); objectui#4048; objectui#4233; homeAffordancesFollowDeclaration-7256; this ruling's maintainer amendment (verbatim in the first line).`

Confidence gap carried: whether `resolveLandingPath`'s dependencies can live inside `app-shell` — that is exactly what decides the direction, and the dev measures it before choosing.

## Execution, same stroke

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. Clause-②: the claiming seat declares from the diff (the console's behaviour does not move; the package export may). `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` untouched.

## ⭐ The ruling's acceptance holds BY CONSTRUCTION, not by assertion

Letter A′ fixed the console's `/` behaviour as the unmoving point. The strongest possible evidence for that is what the diff does not contain, and this seat counted it: **`apps/console` contributes ZERO files.** ⇒ there is no version of 「the console's `/` changed」 that survives the file list.

## ⭐ The confidence gap the ruling named has TWO halves, and they answer differently

The ruling said the direction turns on whether `resolveLandingPath`'s dependencies can live inside `app-shell`. The dev split that into the question asked and the question that matters:

| half | answer | how |
|---|---|---|
| **1. can the dependencies live there?** | **YES, all six** | every symbol the console element imports beyond React is already reachable inside `app-shell` (`useMetadata` via `providers/MetadataProvider`; `LoadingFallback` / `SETUP_APP_PACKAGE_ID` / `SETUP_APP_NAME` from `console/ConsoleShell.tsx`; `RedirectWithSplash`; `MetadataTypeStatus`), zero console-local. ⭐ Control in the same command: an invented seventh name reported absent |
| **2. can it be HOSTED there without losing the acceptance?** | **NO** | measured by probe: element copied into `app-shell`, exported from the barrel, console file reduced to a re-export → `RootLandingRedirect.route.test.tsx` **7 failed / 54 passed**, first failure `expected /home to be /apps/crm_app` |

⚠️ And the mechanism is not a surprise — it is written down in the acceptance instrument's own prose: those routing tests mock `@object-ui/app-shell` **wholesale**, so an element living inside the package reads real hooks the mock never reaches. ⭐ Same-subject control in that run: the pure-policy and both parity tests stayed green.

⇒ 「the dependencies CAN move」 and 「the element MAY move」 are different questions, and answering only the first would have chosen the direction that breaks the ruling's own acceptance. The probe's mutation is proved by blob hash `b4fcc24f` and the restore by blob `2ed110ae` equalling its HEAD blob plus an empty `git status` and the probe module gone — ⛔ never by an exit code.

⇒ Direction taken: **remove the unguarded published twin**; the console's guarded element stays where it is. That is also the less-code side, which is the ruling's stated tie-break.

## Verified by this seat

`RootRedirect`'s only real in-repo **import** on `origin/main` is `examples/console-starter/src/App.tsx:21` — every other hit is prose, a comment, or the 7373 scan's own regex (`ROOT_REDIRECT_BODY`). ⭐ Control lit in the same command: `RootLandingRedirect`, the guarded twin, returns hits across `apps/console`, so the instrument finds this class of symbol. ⇒ the single consumer the PR re-routes is the single consumer there is.

The new pin `rootLandingHasOneResolver-10042.test.ts` is RED before the removal (2 failed / 2 passed, ⭐ **its control case green**, so the reader was known to discriminate) and GREEN after. ⇒ 「exactly one resolver」 is now enforced rather than intended.

## Readings recorded, ⛔ neither treated as a pass

- `packages/app-shell`: 739 files, 7,323 passed, 1 skipped, **1 failed** — `AppContent.inaccessibleAppStrand.test.tsx`, ⛔ **not in this diff** (control: the diff's nine paths listed in the same command, zero match), failing on the repo's documented network-escape class (objectui#6640 / #7439) and passing 6/6 re-run alone.
- `check:readme-exports` first answered with 8 unjudgeable self-imports against unbuilt dists — recorded as a **prerequisite gap, ⛔ not a verdict** — then built and re-run over a whole population (0 unbuilt). Same for the console's first `type-check`. ⭐ The re-run is the verdict; the first answer is not quietly promoted.

## One follow-up, ⛔ correctly not folded in

`.claude/skills/objectui-contributor/guides/console-development.md` names `RootRedirect` in its route-tree diagram (`:63`) and in its list of importable published building blocks (`:67`) — both of which this PR falsifies, so a reader copying that import list now gets a compile error. ⭐ Verified at those two lines by this seat.

⛔ Deliberately not fixed here: it is a **governed surface**, and one file from there forks this whole PR onto the governed landing path — which AGENTS.md says to split. ⇒ a card follows; landing it is a separate, governed PR that this seat does ⛔ not merge.

Two pending changesets narrate `RootRedirect` as a component that exists and will ship in the same release as its removal. ⛔ Left alone: another card's unreleased narrative, `check:changeset-claims` is report-only and green, and the successor is named — the seat that versions the next release reads every pending changeset anyway.
